message.content: {"paragraphs":[{"criterion":"criterion_1","text":"Your reasoning explains what the key does but never says why a retry is risky in the first place: a timeout doesn't tell the client whether the first charge went through. The retry only happens in the `Err(Error::Timeout)` arm, so the first request may already have been processed by the provider before the client gave up. That uncertainty is the reason a fresh `OperationKey` could cause a second charge, and meeting this criterion means saying that the first charge might have succeeded despite the timeout.","citations":[{"path":"src/payments/retry.rs","first_line":2,"last_line":6}]},{"criterion":"criterion_2","text":"The evaluator couldn't tell whether your reasoning fully connects the reused key to the provider's at-most-once behaviour. Meeting this criterion means saying that the provider recognises a key it has already seen and returns the first charge's receipt instead of charging again. The `charge` doc comment states this directly, and the changed lines send `original.key.clone()` on the retry so that the provider sees the same key as in the first request.","citations":[{"path":"src/payments/client.rs","first_line":12,"last_line":13},{"path":"src/payments/retry.rs","first_line":4,"last_line":6}]}]}
